blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Citizenship Act of 1955 provides for the acquisition and loss of Indian citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution.
Five distinct modes exist for acquiring citizenship: By Birth, By Descent, By Registration, By Naturalisation, and By Incorporation of Territory.

Three distinct modes exist for losing citizenship: By Renunciation (voluntary declaration), By Termination (acquiring foreign citizenship), and By Deprivation (compulsory termination by the Central Government).
Parliament holds exclusive power under Article 11 to regulate citizenship rights, amend the Act, and determine eligibility criteria.
The provisions for Commonwealth Citizenship originally contained in the Act were repealed by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003.
Citizenship is exclusively listed under the Union List (Entry 17) in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India.
Children of foreign diplomats stationed in India and enemy aliens cannot acquire Indian citizenship by birth.
Deprivation is a compulsory termination of Indian citizenship by the Central Government if citizenship was obtained by fraud or if the citizen shows disloyalty to the Constitution of India.
